claims.statement: The European Commission states that the definitive CBAM regime applies from 1 January 2026 and that importers above the stated 50-tonne threshold must seek authorized CBAM declarant status.
Authorized declarants buy CBAM certificates, whose price is linked to EU ETS auction prices, making import records and emissions values inputs to a recurring monetary exposure.
The Commission says declarants can retrieve information supplied by non-EU installation operators through the CBAM Registry, supporting an evidence-exchange workflow tied to named installations.

contrary_evidence: Large customs and ESG software suites already cover CBAM reporting, and recent simplifications reduce the number of affected small importers.
Registry improvements may absorb basic evidence exchange, leaving value only in cross-system reconciliation and supplier operations.

economics.acquisition_route: Recruit two Polish customs agencies in one material vertical, offer a retrospective 2026 evidence-gap audit, then expand within their importer portfolios
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 90 importers at 75,000 PLN blended ARR yields roughly 6.75m PLN ARR by years 4-6. At 18-28% operating margin and majority ownership, retained earnings plus a 4-6x vertical-software valuation could exceed 5m PLN founder net worth in years 5-7.
economics.founder_time: 18-22 hours weekly during the first vertical build; use a contract customs specialist for bounded interpretation
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 72-86%; software matching is high-margin, while technical verification is referred or separately contracted rather than absorbed
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 4-8 months on channel-led mid-market accounts after integration; 9-15 months for direct enterprise accounts
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 3,000-12,000 PLN monthly per importer plus 4,000-20,000 PLN supplier-onboarding projects or a volume tier tied to covered tonnes
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every covered import changes certificate exposure, while supplier evidence and annual declarations recur; accumulated lineage makes replacement costly

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Permissioned graph of installations, products, evidence lineage and discrepancy outcomes; reusable verified supplier packets lower marginal onboarding cost and improve anomaly benchmarks
fingerprint.customer: Polish and EU mid-market CBAM importers and the customs representatives that serve them, initially in a single material category
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: White-label through customs agencies and indirect representatives that already touch every covered entry, supplemented by supplier-facing upload links
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Vertical compliance-reconciliation SaaS plus paid evidence-onboarding, priced by importer, supplier and annual covered tonnes
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Importer pays when its declarations and certificate accruals are continuously reconciled; customs agency can resell a portfolio workspace
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A customs entry creates a certificate exposure but supplier emissions evidence, installation identity or carbon-price data is absent or disagrees with the import record

founder_fit: Quantitative carbon-liability reconciliation is a strong data-science and finance fit.
A single-material, file-first pilot is feasible inside the capital and time limits.
Channel-led customs distribution avoids building a public personal brand.
risks: Bad emissions mappings can create financial and compliance exposure.
One-material specialization can constrain near-term market size.
Regulatory amendments may change thresholds, fields or certificate timing.

structure.commercial_archetype: Regulatory evidence network with reconciliation SaaS
structure.control_point: Month-end CBAM liability accrual and annual declaration/certificate-surrender readiness
structure.critical_dependency: Stable access to customs data, CBAM Registry workflows and credible technical verification partners for emissions evidence

thesis: Offer EU importers and indirect customs representatives a transaction-level ledger that binds customs entries, supplier installation evidence, verified embedded-emissions values, carbon price paid abroad, purchase invoices and CBAM certificate accruals. It flags missing or inconsistent evidence before month-end and produces a review packet for the authorized declarant. Start with Polish importers of one material class and distribute through customs agencies; later, reuse supplier evidence across consenting importers and turn evidence quality into a defensible network. The service supports, but does not act as, the declarant or provide legal advice.
title: CBAM Evidence-to-Certificate Reconciler
uncertainties: Count of Poland-based mid-market importers above the current threshold by material
How much customs agencies will pay versus bundle into representation fees
Permission model for reusing supplier evidence across importers
